title: The Green New Deal and the Future of Carbon Pricing
venue: Journal of Policy Analysis and Management
abstract: In this article, we discuss the future of U.S. climate policy within the context of the Green New Deal (GND). The GND has many features and this article is not meant to provide a comprehensive evaluation of all components of it. Rather, we focus on carbon pricing and whether it, rather than mandates and standards, should feature more centrally in the future of U.S. climate policy. We orient our discussion around issues related to theoretical aspects of different climate policy instruments and empirical evidence on their performance. We consider the efficiency and effectiveness of different approaches, their distributional aspects and how these relate to the increasingly important environmental justice priorities, and their political feasibility.
abstract_zh: 在本文中，我们在绿色新政（GND）的背景下讨论美国气候政策的未来。绿色新政包含诸多内容，本文并非旨在对其所有组成部分作全面评估。相反，我们聚焦于碳定价，探讨在美国气候政策的未来中，碳定价是否应当比强制性规定与标准发挥更为核心的作用。我们围绕不同气候政策工具的理论层面以及其绩效的实证证据展开讨论。我们考察不同方案的效率与有效性、它们的分配效应，以及这些分配效应如何与日益重要的环境正义优先事项相关联，并考察其政治可行性。

Who Wins in an Energy Boom? Evidence from Wage Rates and Housing
abstract: This article presents evidence on the distributional effects of energy extraction by examining the effect of the recent U.S. energy boom on wage rates and housing. The boom increased local wage rates in almost every major occupational category. The increase occurred regardless of whether the occupation experienced a corresponding change in employment, suggesting a tighter labor market that benefited local workers. Wage rates also increased substantially across the entire wage rate distribution, although the percentage increase was slightly higher at the bottom of the distribution than at the top. Local housing values and rental prices both increased, thereby benefiting landowners. For renters, the increase in prices was completely offset by a contemporaneous increase in income. The results suggest that bans on drilling have negative monetary consequences for a large share of local residents. (JEL J23, Q33, R31)
abstract_zh: 本文通过考察近期美国能源繁荣对工资率和住房的影响，提供了能源开采分配效应的证据。这一繁荣使几乎所有主要职业类别的当地工资率均有所上升。无论该职业的就业是否发生相应变化，工资上涨都会出现，这表明劳动力市场趋紧，并使当地工人受益。工资率在整个工资分布上也显著上升，尽管分布底部的涨幅略高于顶部。当地住房价值和租金均有所上涨，从而使土地所有者受益。对于租房者而言，租金上涨被同期收入的增长完全抵消。研究结果表明，禁止钻探会对当地很大一部分居民的货币收入产生负面影响。（JEL J23, Q33, R31）

title: Explaining Demand for Green Electricity Using Data from All U.S. Utilities
Improving Energy Codes
abstract: Energy codes set efficiency standards for buildings in the majority of U.S. states. Under most energy codes, builders can comply by demonstrating that the projected private expenditures on energy bills for a proposed building are less than a certain threshold. Using theory and evidence, I show that energy codes would be improved if compliance was instead determined by the projected social damages. Relative to current practice, damage-based codes would likely provide stronger incentives for electricity than natural gas conservation, in most states. Implementation of damage-based codes would lead to substantial welfare gains.
abstract_zh: 能源规范（energy codes）在美国大多数州为建筑设定了能效标准。在大多数能源规范下，建筑商只要证明拟建建筑的预计私人能源账单支出低于某一阈值即可达标。运用理论与证据，我表明：若改为以预计社会损害作为达标判定依据，能源规范将得到改善。相较于现行做法，在大多数州，基于损害的规范对电力节约的激励可能强于对天然气节约的激励。实施基于损害的规范将带来可观的福利收益。

Are Building Codes Effective at Saving Energy? Evidence from Residential Billing Data in Florida
abstract: We evaluate the effect of a change in the energy code applied to buildings using residential billing data on electricity and natural gas, combined with data on observable characteristics of each residence. The study is based on comparisons between residences constructed just before and after an increase in the stringency of Florida's energy code in 2002. We find that the code change is associated with a decrease in the consumption of electricity by 4% and natural gas by 6%. We estimate average social and private payback periods that range between 3.5 and 6.4 years.
abstract_zh: 我们利用居民电力和天然气的账单数据，结合每处住宅可观测特征的数据，评估建筑所适用的能源规范变更的效果。研究基于对2002年佛罗里达州能源规范提高严格程度前后分别建成的住宅之间的比较。我们发现，此次规范变更与电力消费下降4%、天然气消费下降6%相关。我们估算的平均社会和私人投资回收期在3.5至6.4年之间。
